$comment: Mid-century Modernism type direction. Fonts come from foundations/typography/source/pairings.json plus the newPairings below (Google Fonts only); this file says which suit this approach and how to set them. Sizes are rules of thumb unless a source is given. Designer credits come from the google/fonts repository (METADATA.pb and DESCRIPTION files).
character: Heavy geometric or grotesque sans headlines, set tight, next to a warm old-style serif for subheads and body: the mix of Futura-family modernism and Caslon-style advertising lettering seen on 1950s book jackets, record sleeves and ads. Letter-spaced capitals for small labels. Hand-lettering appears, but drawn for the piece, not as a font.

anatomy.$comment: What to look for when judging a typeface for this approach.

construction.want: Geometric (circle-based o, single-storey a optional) or a sturdy grotesque
construction.why: Matches the ruler-and-compass shapes of the art; Futura-family sans were the period's modern voice.

weight.why: Heavy headlines hold their own beside flat colour shapes, and their stems echo the structural key line.

contrast.want: Low in the sans; moderate in the serif
contrast.why: Sans and art read as one printed plate; the serif brings the warmth of advertising lettering.

serif.want: Old-style or Caslon-like, with a lively italic
serif.why: Italic subheads were a common companion to geometric headlines on book jackets and ads.

quirks.want: One or two characterful letters (a pointed A or M, a tall ascender)
quirks.why: A little personality without novelty; the playfulness lives in the art.

avoid: Art deco display faces (they belong to the 1920s-30s Commercial Modernism style)
Swiss neo-grotesques used alone for warm work (too cold for the American side of the style)

fit.$comment: core = recommended, good = works, accent = special cases, avoid = not for this approach.

bricolage-figtree.why: Bricolage Grotesque cites Antique Olive (Excoffon, 1960s) among its influences; its irregular, characterful forms feel hand-cut and period-right without pastiche.

young-onest.why: Young Serif's heavy, soft old-style forms suit the friendly Flora and Blair side of the style; pair with a geometric headline elsewhere if needed.

fraunces-commissioner.why: Fraunces's soft, chunky serif recalls mid-century advertising lettering; keep to one weight and avoid the 'wonky' extras.

schibsted.why: A sturdy grotesque: the Swiss side of the period. Works for Lustig- or Eames-like restraint; add warmth through the art.

instrument.why: The condensed serif suits bookish Lustig-style covers and editorial pieces, but its contemporary elegance is less period.

source.why: Very readable but neutral; use for text-heavy products where the art carries the style.

plex.why: Engineered, corporate-modern feel fits Eames- or IBM-era technical products only.

nunito.why: Rounded app-like terminals read as 2010s UI, not mid-century print.

alegreya.why: Calligraphic Renaissance forms point to a different tradition.

spartan-caslon.why: New pairing: geometric sans headlines over Caslon-style advertising text, the core sound of the style.

boogaloo-jost.why: New pairing: 1960s album-cover lettering for short headlines with a Futura-like sans for everything else.

newPairings.name: Mid-century Advertising
newPairings.mood: Confident and warm. A heavy geometric sans in the American Spartan and Futura tradition over a Caslon drawn from 1950s advertising lettering, with a lively italic for subheads.
newPairings.bestFor: Most mid-century work: posters, book and packaging design, websites, editorial.

display.case: Sentence case; letter-spaced capitals for labels
display.designer: Matt Bailey, Tyler Finck (The League of Moveable Type)
display.notes: The League of Moveable Type's interpretation of Matt Bailey's Spartan, based on early 20th-century American geometric sans serifs (ATF and Linotype Spartan were Futura competitors).

body.notes: Based on hand-lettering artists' interpretations of Caslon typical of 1950s advertising, not on 18th-century specimens. Companion display family: Libre Caslon Display (Impallari Type).

newPairings.name: Album Cover
newPairings.mood: Playful and loud for a few words, calm for the rest. Boogaloo's drawn letters follow 1960s LP-cover lettering; Jost is a clean Futura-style sans for everything else.
newPairings.bestFor: Music, food, events, children's products, packaging; short headlines only.

display.case: Sentence case; headlines of six words or fewer
display.notes: Structure of classic American lettering found on 1960s LP covers of Latin music. Single weight; never for body or more than one line of six words.

body.notes: Inspired by 1920s German sans serifs (the Futura tradition); variable since 2020 with Mirko Velimirovic.

typeWithArt.weightMatch: Headline stems should be close to the structural key line (about 1.25% of the artboard's short side at headline size); contours stay thinner than the type.
typeWithArt.scaleMatch: Headline cap height 1/4 to 1/2 of the emblem's height: the emblem leads, the headline names it.
typeWithArt.alignment: Left-aligned text block on the side opposite the emblem; one short line may be centred on an emblem-centre poster.
typeWithArt.registration: Type is printed on the key plate: never misregistered, never textured.
typeWithArt.handLettering: One or two words per piece may be hand-drawn (cut paper or brush) for the piece itself; all other text uses the pairing.

sizes.$comment: Headline cap height as a share of the canvas height, and body text minimums. Rules of thumb.
sizes.viewingDistance: Sign-industry rule of thumb: about 1 inch (25 mm) of letter height for every 10 feet (3 m) of viewing distance for basic legibility; double it for comfortable reading.

measure.source: Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style

setting.case: Sentence case for headlines and text. Letter-spaced capitals for labels of one to three words (wider than usual, a period trait). All-lowercase only inside a logo or wordmark.
setting.italic: The serif italic is the subhead voice: one line or two, never whole paragraphs.
setting.rag: Ragged right; no justified text; avoid single words on the last line of headlines (use text-wrap: balance).
setting.numbers: Use the mono for dates, times, prices and codes.

rules: Heavy geometric sans headline, old-style serif or Futura-style sans text.
Three sizes and two weights per piece.
Labels in widely letter-spaced capitals; everything else in sentence case.
Type sits on the key plate: never misregistered or textured.
No handwriting fonts; hand-lettering only when drawn for the piece.
